title: Electronic state of vortices at twin boundaries in a nematic superconductor
authors: Keita Goto, Hiroto Adachi, Masanori Ichioka
abstract: Local electronic states of vortices in an s $\pm$ d wave nematic superconductor are studied both in the absence and presence of twin boundaries. The Bogoliubov-de Gennes theory for a tight-binding model is used with its nematicity represented by the anisotropy in the transfer integrals and attractive interactions between the nearest-neighbor sites. We evaluate s and d wave components of the pair potentials and the local density of states, and analyze the effects of nematicity on the vortex core structures with/without twin boundaries. We find that a single vortex trapped at the twin boundary is composed of a bound pair of fractional vortices accompanied by weakly-induced s $\pm$ id wave components, despite that such s $\pm$ id wave components do not appear in a zero magnetic field. The calculated spatial structures of the local electronic states are compared with the vortex image measured by STM experiments in an iron-based superconductor FeSe.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the electronic structure of vortices situated at twin boundaries in a nematic superconductor using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes theory. The research finds that the boundary induces fractional vortices and novel s +/- id wave components in the superconducting order parameter. This provides crucial insights into how structural defects interact with complex pairing symmetries in correlated superconducting materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the local electronic states of vortices when they are trapped at twin boundaries within a nematic superconductor.
main_result: The trapping of a single vortex at a twin boundary results in a bound pair of fractional vortices accompanied by weakly-induced s +/- id wave components, even though these components are absent in zero magnetic field.
method: The authors employed the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) theory using a tight-binding model to calculate the local density of states (LDOS) and pair potentials.
model_or_system: The system is a nematic superconductor, modeled on a square lattice with nematicity introduced via anisotropy in transfer integrals and attractive interactions. The superconductivity is described by an s +/- d wave pairing potential.
key_observables: Local density of states (LDOS), pair potential components (s and d wave), and the vortex core structure.
important_parameters: Nematic anisotropy, twin boundary structure, and the superconducting gap parameters ($\Delta_s, \Delta_d$).
main_assumptions: The model uses a simple tight-binding approximation and assumes spin-singlet pairing; it also notes that the model might fail to capture the full complexity of time-reversal symmetry breaking at the boundary.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spatial structure of the pair potential components and the LDOS spectra, comparing vortex states with and without twin boundaries.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework (BdG theory, tight-binding model) and then analyzing the electronic states in different regimes: first, the vortex state without boundaries, followed by the analysis of the twin boundary state, culminating in the combined vortex-at-twin-boundary case.
why_interesting: The study of exotic superconducting phases, such as those exhibiting nematicity and complex pairing symmetries (like s +/- id), is highly relevant to understanding unconventional superconductivity in materials like iron-based superconductors, which often involve strong electronic correlations.
